# DSH Spark Insights
**English** | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that reads spark performance exports from Minecraft servers and give
s the agent two read-only tools for performance analysis.
## Features

- Parses spark protobuf exports:
- `.sparkprofile` — execution, allocation, and lock sampler data
-

`.sparkheap` — heap summaries
- raw spark health data (reports platform statistics only)
- gzip-wrap

ped exports
- legacy spark data with nested `children` / `time` fields
- Schema-generated decoder fo

r current spark fields, with a hand-written
fallback for legacy layouts
- Performance overview: plat

form/version, TPS, MSPT, CPU, heap/non-heap memory, GC, disk, players, uptime, world counts
- Sample

r analysis:
- thread-group totals with a wait / ≈on-CPU split (kernel-wait frames excluded), merge c

ounts, and top-frame attribution
- top methods by self and inclusive time
- searchable call tree
- p

er-window hotspots when the profile has per-window stack times
- tick-window TPS / MSPT / CPU / enti

ties / chunks, with a CPU-use fallback ordering when the platform records no tick statistics
- plugi

n/mod source attribution
- Time-series metrics, plugin/mod metadata, world details, memory pools, ne

twork interfaces, and ping
- Heap analysis by class size or instance count
- Automatic Mojang mappin

gs for obfuscated profiles (see Mappings)
- Results are cached per file version (two files), and no
file contents leave the machine.
## Supported platforms
Any platform that produces spark's common protobuf format works: Paper, Spigot, Fabric, NeoForge, pr
oxies, and the extra-platform builds.
### Nukkit
spark-nukkit uses `spark-common`, so its `.sparkprofile` and `.sparkheap` files are the same format
and need no conversion.
The Nukkit build currently does not implement tick hooks/reporters, so its exports have **no TPS/MSP
T and no tick counts**; window statistics fall back to fixed time buckets that carry CPU use, and th
e tool orders and labels them accordingly. CPU, memory, GC, threads, stack hotspots, inclusive time,
source attribution, and heap summaries still work. The report explicitly notes the missing tick sta
attribution, and heap summaries still work. The report explicitly notes the missing tick statistics.

## Tools
### `spark_analyze`
Returns a performance overview: metadata, performance snapshot, metric trends, plugins/mods, world a
nd system details, thread totals, hotspots, worst tick windows, plugin attribution, and heap informa
stem details, thread totals, hotspots, worst tick windows, plugin attribution, and heap information.
| Parameter | Meaning |

| `file_path` | spark export path; relative paths use the session working directory |
| `mappings_pa

th` | optional Mojang ProGuard mappings file (see Mappings) |
| `thread` | optional thread group nam
e or substring; defaults to the server main thread ("Server thread", "main", …), else the thread wit

h the most on-CPU time (kernel waits excluded) |
| `limit` | hotspot rows, 1–50, default 10 |
### `spark_query`
| `view` | Result |

| `methods` | methods sorted by self or inclusive time; supports `query` |
| `threads` | all thread

groups, sorted by on-CPU time (kernel waits excluded) |
| `tree` | call tree; `query` locates a clas
s/method, `depth` controls levels below a match, `limit` raises the line budget (default 120, max 30

0) |
| `windows` | tick windows; `sort=time` or `sort=worst` (worst falls back from MSPT to TPS to C

PU process use when tick statistics are missing) |
| `sources` | plugin/mod source attribution |
| `

metrics` | spark metric series (TPS, MSPT, CPU, memory, allocation, world, ping) |
| `plugins` | plu

gin/mod name, version, author, builtin flag |
| `world` | entity types, worlds, chunks, game rules,

data packs |
| `system` | CPU, heap, memory pools, network interfaces, OS/Java/JVM, ping |
| `heap`
| heap classes; `sort=size` or `sort=instances` |

`spark_query` accepts the same `file_path` and optional `mappings_path` as
`spark_analyze` (see Mapp

ings), plus `view`, `query`, `window`,
`depth`, `sort`, and `limit` as listed above.

`methods`, `tree`, and `sources` accept `window` (1-based tick-window index) to
analyze only that wi
ndow when the profile contains per-window stack times.

## Mappings

Profiles whose sampled frames still use ProGuard-obfuscated names (typically a
vanilla server; e.g.

`agh.a`) are remapped to Mojang's official names
automatically — in hotspots, the call tree, source

attribution, and heap
tables. Frames that already use readable class names (Paper, Spigot,
Forge/Neo

Forge, Fabric, proxies) are detected from the frames themselves, so
they never trigger a version-cac

he lookup or download; a co-located mapping
file is still honored when the platform itself is not sk

ipped outright.
Resolution order:

1. an explicit `mappings_path` argument pointing at a ProGuard mapping file
(Mojang's `server.txt` /

`client.txt` for the matching version);
2. a sibling file next to the export: `<export>.mappings`,

gs/<version>.txt` —
downloaded mappings are stored here, and you can also drop files in
yourself (us

eful for air-gapped machines);
4. an automatic download from Mojang's piston-meta service for the pr

ofile's
Minecraft version, written back to the cache so later lookups reuse it
(two concurrent first
-time lookups for the same version may both fetch).

Every mapping file is parsed and validated first: a file that is not a
ProGuard mapping (a stray `se

rver.txt`, a JSON source map, a reversed mapping
file) is ignored — or reported when passed explicit

ly — instead of being
applied or blocking the cache/download.

Downloads share one 25-second budget, are validated before they are cached,
